newsitem.title: USA: U.S. grain dealers take 20 cts soy protection.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grain dealers take 20 cts soy protection.

text.p: Weekend rain was expected to cause a sharply lower futures open Monday and Midwest grain dealers were taking 20 cents per bushel cash price protection on soybeans and eight cents on corn in response.
"Looks like we got some rain so we're taking protection this morning," one Illinois merchandiser said.
In response to the Midwest rains, soybean futures were expected to open 15 to 20 cents per bushel lower, corn was seen seven to 12 cents lower and wheat was seen three to five cents lower.
Some grain dealers said that they were dropping their basis bids in line with Project A overnight trade instead of taking protection, and others were bidding for corn basis only.
